## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $a,\mu,\rho_0>0$, $p_\infty\in\mathbb R$, $U\in\mathbb R^3$, and $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$. On the exterior domain $\Omega_a=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:r=|x|>a\}$ put $s=U\cdot x$ and define

$$u(x)=A(r)U+B(r)sx,\qquad A(r)=1-\frac{3a}{4r}-\frac{a^3}{4r^3},\qquad B(r)=-\frac{3a}{4r^3}+\frac{3a^3}{4r^5},\qquad p(x)=p_\infty-\frac{3\mu a}{2}\frac{s}{r^3}.$$

This field is $C^2$ up to the spherical boundary from the exterior, $p$ is $C^1$, $u=0$ at $r=a$, and $u\to U$ uniformly in direction as $r\to\infty$. It satisfies the steady Stokes system $\rho_0^{-1}\nabla p-\nu\Delta u=0$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$ on $\Omega_a$. For $n=x/a$ on $S_a=\{x:|x|=a\}$, put $D u=(\partial_j u_i)_{i,j}$ and form the stress $\sigma=-pI_3+\mu(Du+(Du)^{\mathsf T})$. The formal resultant with this sphere orientation is

$$\int_{S_a}\sigma n\,dS=6\pi\mu aU.$$

Moreover, among classical pairs $(\widetilde u,\widetilde p)$ satisfying the same Stokes system on $\Omega_a$, the same zero boundary velocity and far-field limits, and the uniform decay conditions $\widetilde u-U=O(r^{-1})$, $\nabla\widetilde u=O(r^{-2})$, $\widetilde p-p_\infty=O(r^{-2})$, this pair is unique. Here the velocity is $C^2$ and pressure $C^1$ locally up to $S_a$, the displayed bounds hold uniformly in direction, and pressure is normalized by its limit $p_\infty$. The claim is for the Stokes equations only; it gives no finite-Reynolds-number error bound or exterior Navier–Stokes existence result. Under SI interpretation, $a,r,x$ are in metres, $U$ in metres per second, $\rho_0$ in kilograms per cubic metre, $\mu$ in pascal-seconds, $\nu$ in square metres per second, $p,p_\infty$ in pascals, and the resultant in newtons.

[F1] [[def-fd-x00]]: the constant-density steady Stokes equation is $\rho_0^{-1}\nabla p-\nu\Delta u=0$ with $\nu=\mu/\rho_0$; $D u=(\partial_j u_i)_{i,j}$, $\Delta$ is componentwise, and the stress is $-pI_3+\mu(Du+(Du)^{\mathsf T})$.

[F4] [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]]: a continuous scalar field is integrated against that density on the parameter region; area is the integral of the density, and changing values on a content-zero parameter boundary does not change the integral. ## Proof

1.1 For any radial scalar functions $A,B$, direct Cartesian differentiation with $\partial_i r=x_i/r$ and $\partial_i s=U_i$ gives $\operatorname{div}(AU+Bsx)=(s/r)(A'+r^2B'+4rB)$ and $\Delta(AU+Bsx)=(A''+2A'/r+2B)U+(B''+6B'/r)sx$. For the stated coefficients, $A'=3a/(4r^2)+3a^3/(4r^4)$, $A''=-3a/(2r^3)-3a^3/r^5$, $B'=9a/(4r^4)-15a^3/(4r^6)$, and $B''=-9a/r^5+45a^3/(2r^7)$. Substitution yields $A'+r^2B'+4rB=0$ and $\Delta u=-3aU/(2r^3)+9asx/(2r^5)$. Also $\nabla(s/r^3)=U/r^3-3sx/r^5$, so $\nabla p=\mu\Delta u$ and $\operatorname{div}u=0$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 At $r=a$, $A(a)=B(a)=0$, giving $u=0$. As $r\to\infty$, $A(r)-1=O(r^{-1})$ and $|B(r)sx|=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly because $|s|\le |U|r$; hence $u-U=O(r^{-1})$. Differentiating the displayed radial expression gives $\nabla u=O(r^{-2})$, and $|p-p_\infty|\le (3\mu a|U|)/(2r^2)$; these also establish the required uniform far-field limits. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Let $(\widetilde u,\widetilde p)$ be any other pair in the stated class and put $w=\widetilde u-u$, $q=\widetilde p-p$. Subtracting the equations gives $\operatorname{div}w=0$, $\mu\Delta w=\nabla q$, $w=0$ on $S_a$, and $w=O(r^{-1})$, $\nabla w=O(r^{-2})$, $q=O(r^{-2})$ uniformly. For each $R>a$, apply [F2] on the bounded smooth annulus $\Omega_{a,R}=\{a<r<R\}$ to $qw$ and to $\sum_iw_i\nabla w_i$. ## Postulate

Adopt the mathematical Countable Choice convention: every sequence of nonempty sets admits a choice function. Use the complete Euclidean Lebesgue spaces, measurable maps, almost-everywhere equality and Lebesgue integrals of the conservative weak-form definition. This convention specifies the mathematical weak branch.

Work in a classical Cartesian inertial frame with SI units on a fixed open spatial region $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ and time interval $(0,T_f)$, where $T_f>0$ is measured in seconds. Write $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for functions whose absolute value is integrable on every compact subset. Let all fields be measurable functions of $(t,x)$ on $\Omega\times(0,T_f)$. Space-time integrals use the restriction of $\lambda_4$ to $\Omega\times[0,T_f)$, and initial integrals use the restriction of $\lambda_3$ to $\Omega$; both restrictions use their trace sigma-algebras. The displayed iterated notation uses the completed-product convention, with section integrals for almost every time, as in the conservative weak-form definition. Require $T>0$ almost everywhere wherever $q/T$ or $r/T$ is used. Let $\rho\ge0$ be mass density in kilograms per cubic metre, $u$ velocity in metres per second, $\sigma$ Cauchy stress in pascals, $b$ body acceleration in metres per second squared, $e$ specific internal energy in joules per kilogram, $q$ outward-positive conductive heat flux in watts per square metre, $r$ specific heat supply in watts per kilogram, $T>0$ absolute temperature in kelvins, and $s$ specific entropy in joules per kilogram kelvin. Set $E:=e+|u|^2/2$ in joules per kilogram. Assume these fields are $C^1$ on each side and, for every relatively compact interface patch, admit $C^1$ one-sided extensions to its closed sides; here $C^1$ means that the fields and all their first time and spatial coordinate partial derivatives are continuous on those extensions. $$\partial_t(\rho s)+\operatorname{div}(\rho s u+q/T)\ge\rho r/T.$$

Here $x=(x',x_3)$ and all space-time points in this lemma use time-first coordinates $(t,x)$; the coordinate permutation $(t,x)\mapsto(x,t)$ identifies these fields and tests with the spatial-first domains in the conservative weak-form definition. The minus and plus sides are $\mathcal O^-=\mathcal O\cap\{x_3<h(t,x')\}$ and $\mathcal O^+=\mathcal O\cap\{x_3>h(t,x')\}$. Let $U^\pm,S^\pm$ be $\mathbb R^m$-valued and $F^\pm$ be $\mathbb R^{m\times3}$-valued fields that are $C^1$ on their respective sides and admit $C^1$ one-sided extensions to every relatively compact part of $\Gamma$. For a matrix flux $F$, $F_j\in\mathbb R^m$ denotes its $j$th spatial column and $(\operatorname{div}_xF)_a=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}F_{aj}$. For any one-sided trace $G$, write $[G]=G^+-G^-$. Put $\lambda=\sqrt{1+|\nabla_{x'}h|^2}$, and define the unit normal from minus to plus and its signed normal speed by
$$n=\frac{(-\nabla_{x'}h,1)}{\lambda},\qquad V_n=\frac{\partial_t h}{\lambda}.$$

It holds if and only if $\partial_tU^\pm+\operatorname{div}_xF^\pm=S^\pm$ on both sides and
$$[F]n-V_n[U]=0$$
on $\Gamma$. The initial-data term in the weak initial form is independent; this interior jump condition neither asserts nor requires a strong trace at $t=0$.

For scalar fields $H^\pm,R^\pm$ and vector fluxes $G^\pm$ with the same piecewise $C^1$ regularity, the interior weak inequality $\partial_tH+\operatorname{div}_xG\ge R$ means
$$\int_{\mathcal O}\bigl(H\,\partial_t\psi+G\cdot\nabla_x\psi+R\psi\bigr)\,dx\,dt\le0$$

for every nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^1(\mathcal O)$. It holds if and only if $\partial_tH^\pm+\operatorname{div}_xG^\pm\ge R^\pm$ on both sides and
$$[G]\cdot n-V_n[H]\ge0$$
on $\Gamma$. These are local equivalences for prescribed piecewise-smooth fields, not existence or uniqueness theorems for nonlinear systems. The fields are abstract mathematical variables with no assigned physical units or constitutive model.
